bullets.title: Psychedelic drug helped people with alcohol use disorder reduce drinking, study shows
bullets.note: From the article: “More than 80% of those who were given the psychedelic treatment had drastically reduced their drinking eight months after the study started, compared to just over 50% in the antihistamine (active placebo) control group, according to results published Wednesday in [_JAMA Psychiatry_](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamapsychiatry/fullarticle/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2022.2096?guestAccessKey=e1328a7a-6e79-43f8-ad04-143fd8134839&utm_source=For_The_Media&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=ftm_links&utm_content=tfl&utm_term=082422).” Here’s a snippet of the experience of Jon Kostas, one of the study’s participants: “When he began the psilocybin trial at age 25, he was consuming almost 23 drinks in a single bender.” Flash forward to today, and Jon “has stayed sober since the trial and founded a nonprofit organization for psychedelic mental health research.” Huge kudos to [Dr. Michael Bogenschutz](https://centerforpsychedelicmedicine.org/michael-bogenschutz/), [Dr. Stephen Ross](https://centerforpsychedelicmedicine.org/stephen-ross-md/), and the entire team at the [NYU Langone Health Center for Psychedelic Medicine](https://centerforpsychedelicmedicine.org/).
